text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Interior Minister Robert Lepikson suspects political motives and opposition to planned changes in the police are behind accusations of embezzlement.
- Police director Ain Seppik said he will resign due to lack of political support.
- A couple of dozen people protested at the city council against planned oil exports through a port in northern Tallinn.
- The Evangelical Lutheran Church admits that the popularity of the church has been decreasing during the last six years.
- A captain of a small transport vessel died during an attempt to save the ship, which had a leaky bow door.
- Negotiations between the government and farmers on the introduction of protective tariffs has begun.
- Several large international companies, Tschudi & Eitzen and Jinhui Shipping, are competing in Estonian Shipping Co's privatisation tender.
- Russia's deputy foreign minister rejected claims that the five presidents' meeting in Tallinn meant the forming of an anti-Russian union.
- The new Finest hotel St Barbara will open in central Tallinn. It can take 106 guests in 53 rooms.
